thread:
Liam (AE): Kicking off CatalystOne POC. They want a performance writeup: sustain 5k QPS, p95 <= 180ms for short-gen (avg 40 tokens out, 20 in). Also need an A/B note on reserved vs burst pricing and answers for their security questionnaire. Can we scope infra + test plan today?
Priya (Sales Eng): Important: customer prefers committed pricing if we can guarantee tail. They asked about quantization effects on output quality.
Diego (Perf Eng): Quick checks: 1) seq lengths confirmed? 2) any custom user functions/plugins that add postprocessing latency?
Liam (AE): Seq lengths are typical customer templates: 20 input, 40 output. No extra postprocessing from their side.
Diego (Perf Eng): Ok. Recommendation: Dedicated fleet using bfloat16/INT8 quantized variant of rwd-small-v2, continuous batching with per-request TTL caching. Suggested pool: 6 nodes x 8-GPU instances (each GPU ~A10G-equivalent), batch target 24-48 tokens per batch. Expect average server-side generation latency ~120-140ms under steady load, p95 ~165-190ms depending on KV cache hit rate.
Hana (SRE): A few ops notes: network RTT to their app-hosting (us-east1) ~8-12ms. If we enable VPC peering + private IPs latency drops ~6-8ms. Also recommend enclave-style prewarm to avoid process cold starts.
Olivia (Security): Security Qs: Do they need BYOK (bring-your-own-key) / HSM? Any ePHI concerns? Logging retention limits?
Liam (AE): They're handling PHI, so BYOK + HSM preferred. Require 180-day audit logs retention minimum and region restriction to us-east.
Diego (Perf Eng): Load plan (short):
```
- Smoke (5m): 50 qps, sanity checks, ensure cache primed
- Ramp (20m): 50 -> 5k qps linear, monitor batch sizes and queue latency
- Steady (45m): 5k sustained, collect p50/p95/p99, GPU util, cache hit rate
- Spike sim (4x): 15k qps 90s bursts to validate throttling & queue backpressure
- Scale down (10m): graceful ramp to 0
Metrics: per-GPU throughput (tokens/s), avg batch size, rq queue time, KV hit%
```
Diego (Perf Eng): Use locust with our tokenized prompts for realistic pacing. Example launcher:
```
LOCUSTFILE=tests/locust_catalyst.py locust -f $LOCUSTFILE --host=https://api.redwood.example --users 5000 --spawn-rate 250
```
Priya (Sales Eng): Pricing sketch for proposal doc? Need floor numbers: committed vs on-demand bursts, plus security add-ons.
Diego (Perf Eng): I can do a quick unit-cost model: assume 40 tokens avg * 5k qps * 3600s * 24h = ~1.73B tokens/day (whoa) wait that's 5k qps continuous -> tokens/s = 200k tokens/s -> per day 17.28B tokens. Ok use monthly.
Priya (Sales Eng): Keep it simple in the one-pager. Monthly baseline, reserved discount tiers, burst surcharge %, and logging/KMS add-on line items.
Diego (Perf Eng): Ballpark numbers (to be refined):
- Reserved pool: $48,000 / month (committed)
- On-demand bursts: +45% over baseline token unit cost during burst windows
- Token unit price (reserved): $0.60 per million tokens (example)
- KMS/HSM add-on + audit-log retention overhead: $2,500 / month
Notes: per-token numbers vary with quantization; INT8 reduces GPU cost ~20% but may require a validation eval for quality.
Hana (SRE): Ops constraints: if we enable request-level traces + 180d retention, imagine ~3% CPU/IO overhead and ~0.5% additional storage; include that in the cost appendix.
Olivia (Security): For BYOK/HSM we need customer key rotation policy and contact. Also add diagram for data-in-transit + at-rest keys. I'll draft answers for their questionnaire referencing SOC2 + ISO scope.
Liam (AE): Good. Can we also show a short risk table in the writeup: cold start risk, region egress, model-regression risk with quant?
Diego (Perf Eng): Yup. Draft risk table entries:
- Cold starts: mitigation=pre-warm pods, canary ramping
- Cross-region caching leakage: mitigation=region-scoped caches, disable replication for POC
- Quantization quality: mitigation=run 1k-sample eval vs baseline, rollback path to FP16 model
Priya (Sales Eng): Action items: (1) Diego to run quick staging calibration at 1k/3k/5k and post numbers (2) Hana to assemble warmup/autoscale policies + peering note (3) Olivia to author security questionnaire answers + BYOK flow (4) Liam to assemble cost appendix + share with customer. Target ETA: tomorrow EOD.
bench-bot: bench-runner v2.7 deployed to staging-nodes — harness ready for calibration. :gear:
Diego (Perf Eng): I'll kick off 1k/3k runs now, will paste a short run summary here in ~2 hours.
Liam (AE): Perfect. Once we have calibration numbers I'll book a joint run with CatalystOne for Friday morning. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
